Collection Description
# Notion REST API v1 (`2025-09-03`) — Users & OAuth Automated Test Suite (Lab 03 Consolidated) **Author:** Gabriel Marcos Guaman Ortuño (SQE III — Group 2) **Peer Reviewer (Lab 02 Audit):** Lilian Rosario López Coca **Target SUT:** Notion REST API `https://api.notion.com/v1` (`Notion-Version: 2025-09-03`) **Scope:** `Users` Module (`GET /v1/users/me`, `GET /v1/users/{user_id}`, `GET /v1/users`) & `OAuth 2.0` Module (`POST /v1/oauth/token`, `POST /v1/oauth/revoke`, `POST /v1/oauth/introspect`) + 3 Chained E2E Workflows (`69` HTTP requests, `345` automated assertions). --- ## Step-by-Step Credential Provisioning & Environment Setup Guide Before executing this collection in Postman Collection Runner or Newman CLI, import `Notion_Users_OAuth_Env.postman_environment.json` and configure the following variables under **Current Value**: ### 1. Primary Internal Integration Token (`NOTION_TOKEN`) 1. Navigate to the [Notion Developers Portal](https://www.notion.so/profile/integrations) and click **New integration**. 2. Select your target Notion test workspace, set the integration type to **Internal**, and enable: - **Content Capabilities:** `Read content`, `Update content`, `Insert content`. - **User Capabilities:** `Read user information including email addresses` (mandatory for `GET /v1/users` and `GET /v1/users/{user_id}`). 3. Copy the generated **Internal Integration Secret** (`ntn_...`) and paste it into the `NOTION_TOKEN` environment variable. 4. Open your Notion workspace, invite at least one workspace member, open your root test page, and connect the integration via **`•••` → `Connections` → Select your integration**. ### 2. Restricted Internal Integration Token (`RESTRICTED_TOKEN`) 1. In the Notion Developers Portal, create a second **Internal Integration** in the same workspace. 2. Under **User Capabilities**, explicitly select **`No user information`** and save. 3. Copy its secret (`ntn_...`) into `RESTRICTED_TOKEN`. This credential is required by `TC_USR_GET_006` to deterministically verify `403 Forbidden` (`code: "restricted_resource"`). ### 3. Public OAuth 2.0 Credentials (`OAUTH_CLIENT_ID`, `OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET`, `OAUTH_REDIRECT_URI`) 1. In the Notion Developers Portal, create or convert an integration to a **Public Integration**. 2. Register the Redirect URI `https://localhost:3000/auth/notion/callback` and set `OAUTH_REDIRECT_URI` to match. 3. Copy the **OAuth client ID** and **OAuth client secret** from the integration's **OAuth Domain & URIs** tab into `OAUTH_CLIENT_ID` and `OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET` (used by the `02_OAuth_Module` folder for RFC 7617 HTTP Basic Authentication). 4. Authorize the integration via the Notion OAuth authorization URL to obtain: - A single-use authorization code (`OAUTH_AUTH_CODE`) for `TC_OAUTH_TOK_001`. - An active OAuth bearer session (`OAUTH_ACCESS_TOKEN`) and refresh token (`OAUTH_REFRESH_TOKEN`) for token rotation, introspection, and revocation scenarios. ### 4. Unattended Execution via Newman CLI ```bash npx newman run labs/lab03/postman/gabriel_guaman/Notion_Users_OAuth_GabrielGuaman.postman_collection.json \ -e labs/lab03/postman/gabriel_guaman/Notion_Users_OAuth_Env.postman_environment.json \ --delay-request 350 \ -r cli,htmlextra \ --reporter-htmlextra-export labs/lab03/reports/Notion_Users_OAuth_GabrielGuaman_Report.html ```
